{{Quote|I'm not putting anyone else in danger, Owen. We're enough. You and me.|Beru Lars to her husband, Owen Lars|<ref name="Part VI">{{Kenobi|Part VI}}</ref>}}
'''Beru Whitesun Lars''', [[Reproduction|born]] '''Beru Whitesun''', was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] from the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. She was [[Marriage|married]] to [[Owen Lars]], the [[Lars family|stepbrother]] of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], the [[Chosen One]], whose [[Skywalker family|son]], [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]], they raised after his father turned to the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side of the force]] and his [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|mother]] [[Death|died]] in childbirth.

In [[1 BBY]], the Lars family purchased two [[droid]]s who, unbeknownst to them, possessed stolen [[Death Star plans|plans]] for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] planet-destroying [[battle station]]. Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s tracked the droids to Lars' homestead, where they interrogated and murdered both her and her husband. When Skywalker discovered that his family had been killed, he left Tatooine with Kenobi to train as a Jedi, joining the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and destroying the Death Star in the [[Battle of Yavin]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
During her youth,<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV">{{StoryCite|story=Beru Whitesun Lars (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> Beru Whitesun<ref name="Beru DB" /> had a [[dream]] of setting up her own cafe or [[restaurant]] in [[Anchorhead]]. She had this dream because, during her school [[Standard year|years]], she entered in a cooking class, and the [[Unidentified cooking instructor|teacher]] told Whitesun that her [[blue-milk cheese]] was the best he had ever tasted, prompting her to have such dream as the instructor said that it appeared that she was [[Reproduction|born]] to make blue-milk cheese.<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV" />

===Before the Empire===
On a supply run in [[Mos Espa]], Whitesun stopped at [[Watto's junkshop|Watto's junk shop]] to have her portable [[Navigation computer|nav]] fixed. There, the girl met [[Watto]]'s [[Slavery|slave]], [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], who fixed the device for cheap. Sometime later, Whitesun introduced Shmi to [[moisture farmer]] [[Cliegg Lars]], who shortly freed and [[Marriage|married]] Skywalker. Whitesun assisted Skywalker with locating and deprogramming the chips of former slaves, including Skywalker using her scanner, the deprogrammer.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Whitesun eventually fell in love with [[Owen Lars]], son of Cliegg Lars, so they began dating.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Shortly before the [[First Battle of Geonosis|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars]], Shmi Skywalker Lars, Owen's stepmother, was abducted by [[Tusken Raider]]s, an event that [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars|brought]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], Shmi's [[Skywalker family|son]], and [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], to the [[Lars homestead|Lars moisture farm]], where they were received by Cliegg. Skywalker arrived too late to save his mother, who [[Death|passed away]] in his arms, prompting him to slaughter the Tuskens. When he returned, a [[Funeral of Shmi Skywalker Lars|funeral]] was held at the farm.<ref name="Episode II" /> During the funeral, Whitesun served [[blue milk]] and [[cheese]] to everyone.<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV" /> Whitesun continued to support [[White Suns|others]] on Tatooine working to free enslaved people. She fed and comforted newly freed people and their families.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

[[File:Beru_receives_baby_Luke.png|thumb|left|250px|Kenobi hands over an infant Luke to Beru.]]
Three years later, Whitesun had already married Owen and taken on his last name. Both alone after Cliegg's death,<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> Owen and Beru decided to have a child, but problems of infertility precluded them to have one, leading them to consider seeing one of the [[fertility droid]]s at [[Mos Eisley]].<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV" /> When the [[The galaxy|galactic]] conflict came to a close, Beru and Owen became the guardians of their new nephew, [[Luke Skywalker]], after his father turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and became [[Darth]] Vader and his mother died in childbirth. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], the [[Jedi Master]] and friend of Anakin, delivered infant Luke to the Lars homestead.<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> After receiving Luke, Beru told Owen that they would be raising his stepbrother's son as their own.<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV" />

===Raising Skywalker===
====Run-in with the Inquisitorius====
{{Quote|She'll come when the suns go down. Best we get positioned now.|Beru Lars|<ref name="Part VI" />}}
For the next nineteen years, Lars and her husband raised Skywalker like a son. Lars would often defend Skywalker's interests against Owen, who was overprotective of him out of fear that he would follow in Anakin's footsteps and try to become a [[Jedi Knight]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> In [[9 BBY]], Luke and Owen carried out work at the homestead, all the while being observed from a distance by Kenobi, who left some spare parts for a [[Luke Skywalker's T-16 skyhopper model|toy T-16 skyhopper]] for Luke. As they worked, however, Luke ran away from the labor, climbed on top the homestead, and pretended to [[Podracing|podrace]], all while Owen and Beru looked for Luke. Upon spotting Luke, Beru laughed while Owen expressed disappointment.<ref name="Part I">{{Kenobi|Part I}}</ref>

[[File:Owen-fires-at-Reva.png|thumb|right|250px|Reva attacks Owen and Beru]]
Not long after, during his [[Rescue of Princess Leia (9 BBY)|rescue]] of [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan]], Luke's twin sister, Kenobi had set off the wrath of the former [[Inquisitor]] [[Reva Sevander]], who now wanted to kill Luke. Upon being told by Owen, Beru asked how Sevander had found out where they lived, and Owen admitted that he did not know, adding that Kenobi was gone. He then told Beru that they needed to leave the homestead, but Beru asserted that she would not leave her home. Owen told her that, if they stayed, they would need help, but Beru told her husband that they were enough. She then pulled out two [[blaster rifle]]s from the homestead, tossed one to Owen, and the two went to position themselves for Sevander's attack.<ref name="Part VI" />

That night, lying to Luke that [[Tusken Raider|tusken raiders]] were on the hunt along the [[Jundland Wastes]], Owen instructed Luke to run if anything happened. Beru then shared an embrace with Luke, and holding back tears, told her nephew that everything would be all right. Owen and Beru then left Luke to prepare for Sevander's impending arrival. Upon her arrival, Owen and Beru began shooting at Sevander, who dodged the shots with her [[Reva's lightsaber|lightsaber]]. Owen then faced Sevander alone, but when she knocked him down, he called to his wife, informing her that Sevander was on her way to her. Beru managed to distract Sevander long enough for Luke to escape the homestead, but was swiftly knocked down by the former Inquisitor. With Sevander gone, Owen and Beru exited the homestead and began desperately calling out for Luke. Just then, Kenobi returned from his [[Fight on a barren moon|confrontation]] with Darth Vader and landed by the homestead. Beru relayed the news to Kenobi, who went to look in the Dune Sea but was swiftly called back over by Beru, who saw a weeping Sevander carry Luke back to the homestead. While Kenobi consoled Sevander, Owen and Beru carried Luke back home.<ref name="Part VI" />

====The Great Drought and beyond====
A year after the [[Great Drought]], Owen was abducted by the [[Wookiee]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Krrsantan]] for unpaid [[water]] taxes to the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Lars sought after her husband armed with a [[rifle]], telling the young Skywalker to stay safe within the homestead.<ref name="Star Wars 20">[[Star Wars (2015) 20|''Star Wars'' (2015) 20]]</ref>

====Proud aunt====
{{Quote|Luke's just not a farmer, Owen. He has too much of his father in him.|Beru Lars|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
[[File:Beru_at_the_dinner_table.png|thumb|left|250px|Beru trying to convince her husband that Luke cannot stay on the farm forever.]]
In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Twin Suns date">According to ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'', [[Maul]]'s final confrontation with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in "Twin Suns" happened thirty [[Standard year|years]] after Kenobi first saw him on [[Tatooine]]. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates that event to [[32 BBY]], "Twin Suns" is set in [[2 BBY]].</ref> Kenobi, following a [[Mission to Tatooine (Imperial Era)|brief confrontation]] with the former [[Sith apprentice]] [[Maul]], visited the Lars moisture farm but watched from a distance. Kenobi heard Lars calling out to a seventeen-year-old Luke from within the homestead, and saw Skywalker running back toward the house against a binary sunset.<ref name="Twin Suns">{{Rebels|Twin Suns (episode)}}</ref>

By [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> Skywalker, now nineteen, wanted to explore the wider [[galaxy]], having never left [[Tatooine]]. Though Owen refused numerous [[time]]s to let Skywalker go when he wished to leave home and join the [[Imperial Academy|Academy]], Lars convinced her husband to let Skywalker go after staying on for only one more season. This decision coincided with the aftermath of the [[Battle of Scarif|theft]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[Death Star plans|plans]] and Darth Vader's [[Secret mission to Tatooine|capture]] of Princess Leia Organa over Tatooine.<ref name="Episode IV" />

===Death===
{{Quote|If they traced the robots here, they may have learned who they sold them to and that would lead them back—home.|Luke Skywalker upon realizing his aunt and uncle's imminent danger|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
[[File:Torched_homestead.png|thumb|right|250px|Beru and her husband lay dead at the hands of the Empire.]]
Around this time, Skywalker and Owen purchased two [[droid]]s from a [[Jawa]] [[sandcrawler]] that stopped by their homestead. These two droids were the [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]] and the [[astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]], who were being hunted by the Empire. Before dinner, Skywalker cleaned the two droids in the garage where he found a message from Organa meant to be received by Kenobi. Skywalker told his aunt and uncle about this recording at the dinner table which prompted discussion about the relationship between Kenobi and Skywalker's [[Parent|father]]. Owen also discussed Skywalker staying another season on the [[farm]], which Lars intervened and tried to reason with her husband that Skywalker shouldn't stay on the farm forever. In this conversation she likened Skywalker with his father, an idea that Owen was not fond of. After dinner Skywalker returned to the garage and found that R2-D2 had fled the homestead. The next morning Skywalker told Lars that he'd had some chores to do and went with C-3PO to look for R2-D2, who was secretly carrying the stolen Death Star plans. A concerned Owen could not find Luke, who was supposed to have the two droid to the south ridge by midday. He spoke to his wife about it, who told him that Skywalker had left early to complete some chores and that he had taken the two droids with him. While Skywalker was away, however,<ref name="Episode IV" /> [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[stormtrooper]]s, who were searching for plans located in R2-D2's memory banks, were led to the Lars homestead by Owen's purchase of the droids from the Jawas. A [[squad]] of stormtroopers killed Beru and Owen and burned their home.<ref name="USW" />

===Post-mortem===
Beyond from the realm of the living, acknowledging her and her husband's deaths, Beru Whitesun Lars reflected on the role that Skywalker played in her life, remembering herself bustling around the kitchen serving blue milk and haggling Owen to let their nephew attend the Imperial Academy. As she speculated that had Owen let Skywalker go, they could be still alive, Lars remembered various moments of her life, finally resting comfortably with the knowledge that Skywalker went off with Kenobi, met Organa, [[Battle of Yavin|destroyed]] the [[Death Star]] [[battle station]] and saved the galaxy.<ref name="BWL:FaCPoV" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|I guess it's an irony. If the boy was here when the jackboot came down, the Empire would still have a Death Star… But if the family wasn't killed, maybe he'd never have left.|Chelli Lona Aphra|<ref name="Darth Vader 7">[[Darth Vader (2015) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 7]]</ref>}}
Despite the recent loss of his adoptive family, Skywalker did not grieve until soon after the battle, when his love interest, [[Nakari Kelen]], was killed on the planet [[Omereth]]. Kelen's death provided Skywalker a moment to consider his losses, and he wept upon thinking of his uncle and aunt.<ref name="Heir to the Jedi">''[[Heir to the Jedi]]''</ref> Skywalker later returned to Tatooine to recover [[The Journals of Ben Kenobi|Kenobi's journal]], which contained stories of the Jedi's few encounters with the Lars family.<ref name="Star Wars 7">[[Star Wars (2015) 7|''Star Wars'' (2015) 7]]</ref>

In the weeks after the Battle of Yavin, Darth Vader searched for the pilot responsible for destroying the Death Star, discovering that the pilot was the son he never knew he had. Vader, accompanied by [[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra]], revisited the abandoned homestead and followed Skywalker's trail. While assessing the destruction, Aphra speculated that Skywalker might have never left Tatooine, had his family been spared.<ref name="Darth Vader 7" />

==Personality and traits==
In contrast to her husband Owen, who was gruff and harsh, Beru Whitesun Lars was warm and loving. She always tried to spoil Skywalker every time she had a chance. She loved her nephew and regarded him as her son in all but name.<ref name="TLJ Junior Novel">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: A Junior Novel]]''</ref>

Lars was a [[human]]<ref name="Beru SWE" /> [[Gender|female]] who stood at 1.65 [[meter]]s.<ref name="Beru DB" /> She had [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], blue [[eye]]s, and light skin.<ref name="Episode IV" />

==Equipment==
During the Clone Wars, Beru wore light [[Clothing|robes]] in various shades of brown and blue.<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Aunt Beru, the wife of Owen Lars, raised Luke Skywalker as her own after his mother died and father went off the deep end. She's more than an adoptive parent and a moisture farmer, she's one of the few adults who puts up with Luke's constant pining for the Academy.|[[Bonnie Burton]]|<ref name="">{{SWArchive|url=collecting/news/hasbro/f20071205/index.html|text=Checklist: 10 Unlikely Unleashed Figures}}</ref>}}
[[File:Beru.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Shelagh Fraser as Beru]]
The character of Beru Lars has existed in one form or another since the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of "''The Star Wars''" in [[1974]]. In this draft, Beru and Owen Lars are anthropologists; there is also a character named "[[Clieg Whitsun]]." In the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|1975 version of the script]], the Larses own a moisture ranch, but they are the parents of Skywalker's cousin, [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia]]. In a later version, it was finalised that they would be the Aunt and Uncle of Luke Skywalker, and that Beru protects Skywalker from violent outbursts by Owen. By the early [[1976]] version, the element of the Larses being killed by Imperial stormtroopers was added to the story.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

British actress [[Shelagh Fraser]] was cast to play Aunt Beru in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']]. Fraser's first day of shooting was [[April 1]], 1976; the shots of the Lars' charred skeletons were filmed a few days prior. When post-production on the film began, sound mixer Derek Ball traveled to Fraser's house and recorded additional dialogue.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film" /> In the mono soundmix of the first release of ''Star Wars'', different takes for Beru's lines were used. All subsequent home video sound mixes use the same take that was used in the initial theatrical Dolby mixes.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.in70mm.com/news/2003/star_wars/index.htm|text=The Original First-Week Engagements Of "Star Wars"|archivedate=20070825074407}}</ref>

[[File:BeruWhitesunLars.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Bonnie Piesse as Beru]]
On [[July 7]], [[2000]], [[StarWars.com]] announced that sixteen-year-old Australian actress [[Bonnie Maree Piesse]] would be playing the role of a younger Beru in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|Episode II]].<ref name="Casting">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/production/news20000707.html|text=Casting Update: More Local Talent}}</ref> Piesse would approach Beru as being a little shy, the idea being that it was the introduction of Luke into her life that matured her.<ref name="Insider3">{{InsiderCite|58|Bonnie Piesse: Micro Beru}}</ref> [[George Lucas]] wanted to make sure that Beru's costume was similar to the one worn in the first film to help establish a visual connection.<ref name="Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> Her wardrobe was also partially inspired by that of Skywalker's friend Camie in ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Beru DB" /> The first time fans would hear the name "Beru ''Whitesun''" was in [[September]] 2000, when [[Lucasfilm]] began registering [[Wikipedia:Domain name|domain names]] featuring names of characters and other things from the upcoming film.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/episode2/story/lucasfilm_registers_new_episode_ii_domain_names_75320.asp|text=Lucasfilm registers new (Episode II?) domain names!|archivedate=20171006022458}}</ref> This same month, Piesse and the crew were filming the Tatooine scenes in [[Tunisia]].<ref name="Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones" /> Lucas also filmed part of a scene for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|Episode III]] in which a [[Wikipedia:Stand-in|stand-in]] actor playing Obi-Wan delivers baby Luke to Owen, played by [[Joel Edgerton]]. However, this would be changed during the Episode III shoot in September [[2003]]. Lucas filmed [[Ewan McGregor]] handing the baby to Piesse, with Owen being played by a stand-in—Edgerton would be shot and added in almost a year later. Lucas made this change because he "felt it would be better if Luke were handed over to a woman."<ref name="The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> [[Andrea Wagner-Barton]], editor [[Roger Barton]]'s wife, served as a stand-in for Piesse in the scene where Beru holds Luke, as their infant son [[Aidan Barton|Aidan]] was playing Luke, though Bonnie did play Beru in the scene when Obi-Wan hands Luke over to her.<ref name="Bartons">{{WebCite|url=https://www.looper.com/828214/revenge-of-the-siths-baby-luke-and-leia-actor-aidan-barton-talks-star-wars-and-mark-hamill-exclusive-interview|text=Revenge Of The Sith's Baby Luke And Leia Actor Aidan Barton Talks Star Wars And Mark Hamill – Exclusive Interview|author=Harbet, Xandra|date=April 11, 2022|archivedate=20220418144853}}</ref>

===Deleted scenes===
At least one shot of Beru did not make the final [[1977]] cut of ''Star Wars'': before the family dinner scene, there is a shot of Beru filling a pitcher of blue milk from a dispenser in a portion of the kitchen not visible in the film.<ref name="Lost Cut">{{InsiderCite|41|The Evolution of Star Wars: Exploring the Lost Cut|The Evolution of ''Star Wars'': Exploring the Lost Cut}}</ref> Also, a popular production still from the film reveals that the dinner scene was shot, or at least rehearsed, with the family members sitting in different seats than in the film.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://starwarz.com/tbone/life-on-tatooine|text=Life on Tatooine: The Lars Homestead|archivedate=20190930083346}}</ref>

A more substantial Beru scene was cut from ''Attack of the Clones'': after Anakin Skywalker returns to the farm with his mother's body, Beru helps Amidala prepare a meal, featuring blue milk, for Skywalker, having a short conversation with Amidala about Naboo and her own reluctance to travel. Nonetheless, this scene does appear in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://starwarz.com/tbone/return-to-tatooine|text=Return To Tatooine: Beru Whitesun|archivedate=20200727193242}}</ref> A shot of Beru and the Larses waving goodbye to Anakin and Padmé was also shot but not used in the final film.<ref name="Y'all">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/explore/attack/2002/07/imageattack20020723.html|series=Image Attack|text=Y'all Come Back Now}}</ref>

===''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' television series===
{{Quote|So some roles are an easier fit than others. And this one just fits so easily that I didn't feel I had to try too hard to embody her.|Bonnie Piesse on reprising her role as Beru Lars in ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''|<ref name="Bonnie Piesse interview">{{WebCite|url=https://www.elle.com/culture/movies-tv/a40084975/bonnie-piesse-nxivm-star-wars-obi-wan-kenobi|text=Bonnie Piesse Escaped The Cult NXIVM. Now, She's Back In The Star Wars Universe.|author=Pope-Puckett, Lauren|date=2022-05-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Elle (magazine)|Elle]]|archivedate=20220524141703}}</ref>}}
[[File:Beru-OWKPoster.png|thumb|right|170px|Beru Lars character poster for ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'']]
During Piesse's break from acting after escaping from the cult [[Wikipedia:NXIVM|NXIVM]], she received a message from [[Deborah Chow]], the director of the ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'' television series. After realizing the message was for casting, Piesse joined a call from [[Wikipedia:Portugal|Portugal]] and Chow convinced her to return to the role of Beru Lars.<ref name="Bonnie Piesse interview" /> Chow was very excited to bring Edgerton and Piesse back to play Owen and Beru Lars, respectively, and she said their return was part of what made the series special.<ref name="17 year">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/obi-wan-kenobi-ewan-mcgregor-hayden-christensen-cover-story|text=Inside the 17-year journey to reunite Ewan McGregor and Hayden Christensen for ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2022-03-10|archivedate=20220310151626}}</ref> Piesse got to embody Lars in a different way, and her portrayal was a middle space between Lars starting to be a mother and Shelagh Fraser's portrayal in the [[original trilogy]]. Piesse felt like she did not need to try too hard to embody Lars because it was a character that "just fits so easily." Piesse prepared by healing, nourishing, and strengthening herself to have all the energy she needed to be on set.<ref name="Bonnie Piesse interview" /> On [[March 29]], [[2021]], Lucasfilm confirmed Piesse as a cast member of the live-action [[Disney+]] television series ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''.<ref name="SW">{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-series-cast|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Series to Begin Production in April, Cast Revealed}}</ref> Piesse has said she would like to reprise her role in a second season or an adjacent film for ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''.<ref name="Bonnie Piesse interview" />
